question_text:
We have the following engineering stress–strain data for a tensile test on a ductile metal:

| Point | σ (MPa) | ε (in-drawn) |
|–|–:|–:|
| 1 | 100 | 0.000 |
| 2 | 250 | 0.005 |
| 3 | 400 | 0.010 |
| … | … | … |
| 8 |  797 | 0.0075 |
| 9 |  838 | 0.0100 |
| 10|  928 | 0.0150 |
| 11|  997 | 0.0200 |
| 12| 1163 | 0.0400 |
| 13| 1236 | 0.0600 |

For true strain, determine n and K in σₜ = K εₜⁿ.

Give your answer as a tuple (n, k).The units of each required answer are (,MPa), respectively.
response:
Using the plastic-region points (8–13), I converted engineering to true quantities:

- σₜ = σ(1+ε)
- εₜ = ln(1+ε)

then performed a linear regression on ln σₜ vs ln εₜ (since ln σₜ = ln K + n ln εₜ):

| σ (MPa) | ε | σₜ | εₜ |
|–:|–:|–:|–:|
| 797 | 0.0075 | 803.0 | 0.00747 |
| 838 | 0.0100 | 846.4 | 0.00995 |
| 928 | 0.0150 | 941.9 | 0.01489 |
| 997 | 0.0200 | 1016.9 | 0.01980 |
| 1163 | 0.0400 | 1209.5 | 0.03922 |
| 1236 | 0.0600 | 1310.2 | 0.05827 |

The least-squares fit gives slope n = 0.2454 and intercept ln K = 7.8828, so K = e^7.8828 ≈ 2651 MPa.

$$\boxed{(0.245,\ 2651)}$$
